p.src: Overview: We now quantize the normal modes found in the previous lecture and ask what particle states they produce. Each transverse mode is a harmonic oscillator, but its normalization is slightly unfamiliar: exciting mode $n$ raises the light-front energy, and hence the mass-squared level, by $n$ units. The first excited open-string level transforms exactly like the two transverse polarizations of a massless vector. Relativistic consistency therefore fixes the ground-state mass squared to be negative. That state is the bosonic-string tachyon, whose real significance is an unstable vacuum, not a practical faster-than-light particle. Finally, once strings interact, joining and splitting make closed strings unavoidable; the lowest closed- string excitation will be the graviton.

p.src: A massless particle has no rest frame. Its invariant spin label is helicity, the angular momentum along its direction of motion. A photon has only $h=+1$ and $h=-1$; a graviton has only $h=+2$ and $h=-2$. A scalar has one $h=0$ state. The lecture uses reflection symmetry to pair the two helicities. In a chiral theory a single massless irreducible representation may carry only one helicity, so the pairing is an additional symmetry statement rather than a consequence of masslessness alone. (Editorial clarification: The modern little-group classification permits one-helicity massless representations. Parity or an appropriate CPT-complete field content supplies the opposite helicity in the familiar photon and graviton examples.)

ja: したがって我々は三つの連関した結論に到達した。開いた弦を量子化すると、その第一励起準位に質量ゼロのベクトルが生じる。その下のボソン的基底状態は不安定である。そして相互作用は必然的に閉じた弦を導入し、そのスペクトルは重力を含む。次の課題は、欠けているスケールを復元し、閉じた弦の量子化を陽に実行することである。
zh: 因此我们得到了三个相互关联的结论。对开弦进行量子化会在其第一激发能级产生一个无质量矢量；其下方的玻色子基态是不稳定的；而相互作用不可避免地引入闭弦，其谱中包含引力。接下来的任务是恢复缺失的标度，并明确地进行闭弦量子化。
